knowledge:
- key_parameters: FirstMass=MS1 starting mass ;; LastMass=MS1 ending mass ;; MassList=matrix of target m/z and charge states ;; ActivationType=type of fragmentation (e.g., "CID", "HCD", "ETD", "UVPD") ;; maxDeviation=maximum log2 deviation from median injection time allowed during filtering ;; threshold=cutoff value for CV filtering (typically 30%) or relative intensity filtering (typically 0.1) ;; n=number of top conditions to return in bestConditions
- alternatives: None mentioned for method generation or top-down analysis; uses ranger for random forest analysis and external tools like Proteome Discoverer (Xtract) for deconvolution.
- when_to_use: Use when designing high-throughput gas-phase fragmentation experiments on a Thermo Orbitrap Fusion Lumos, or when analyzing multi-modal top-down proteomics datasets to optimize sequence coverage.
- pitfalls: XMLMethodChanger requires the operating system to use a dot (.) as the decimal mark and a comma (,) as the digit group separator. XMLMethodChanger does not create methods de novo and requires a pre-existing template .meth file. For recent data, use conditions="ScanDescription" (default) in readTopDownFiles instead of "FilterString" which is only for older topdownrdata.

workflows.name: method_generation
workflows.intent: Generate instrument method XML files to test multiple fragmentation conditions on a Thermo Orbitrap Fusion Lumos.
input: target_mz_matrix.csv (matrix of target m/z and charge states)
workflows.stages: 1. Define MS1 settings using expandMs1Conditions ;; 2. Define target m/z and charge states ;; 3. Define common settings and expand TMS2 conditions for different activation types (CID, HCD, ETD, UVPD) using expandTms2Conditions ;; 4. Create experiments combining settings using createExperimentsFragmentOptimisation ;; 5. Write XML files using writeMethodXmls ;; 6. Convert XMLs to .meth files using runXmlMethodChanger
workflows.code:
ms1 <- expandMs1Conditions(
    FirstMass=400,
    LastMass=1200,
    Microscans=as.integer(10)
)

## Set TargetMass
targetMz <- cbind(mz=c(560.6, 700.5, 933.7), z=rep(1, 3))

## Set common settings
common <- list(
    OrbitrapResolution="R120K",
    IsolationWindow=1,
    MaxITTimeInMS=200,
    Microscans=as.integer(40),
    AgcTarget=c(1e5, 5e5, 1e6)
)

## Create settings for different fragmentation conditions
cid <- expandTms2Conditions(
    MassList=targetMz,
    common,
    ActivationType="CID",
    CIDCollisionEnergy=seq(7, 35, 7)
)
hcd <- expandTms2Conditions(
    MassList=targetMz,
    common,
    ActivationType="HCD",
    HCDCollisionEnergy=seq(7, 35, 7)
)
etd <- expandTms2Conditions(
    MassList=targetMz,
    common,
    ActivationType="ETD",
    ETDReactionTime=as.double(1:2)
)
etcid <- expandTms2Conditions(
    MassList=targetMz,
    common,
    ActivationType="ETD",
    ETDReactionTime=as.double(1:2),
    ETDSupplementalActivation="ETciD",
    ETDSupplementalActivationEnergy=as.double(1:2)
)
uvpd <- expandTms2Conditions(
    MassList=targetMz,
    common,
    ActivationType="UVPD"
)

## Create experiments with all combinations of the above settings
## for fragment optimisation
exps <- createExperimentsFragmentOptimisation(
    ms1=ms1, cid, hcd, etd, etcid, uvpd,
    groupBy=c("AgcTarget", "replication"), nMs2perMs1=10, scanDuration=0.5,
    replications=2, randomise=TRUE
)

## Write experiments to xml files
writeMethodXmls(exps=exps)

## Run XMLMethodChanger
runXmlMethodChanger(
    modificationXml=list.files(pattern="^method.*\\.xml$"),
    templateMeth="TMS2IndependentTemplateForTD.meth",
    executable="path\\to\\XmlMethodChanger.exe"
)

workflows.name: fragmentation_analysis
workflows.intent: Process, filter, aggregate, and analyze top-down proteomics fragmentation data to find optimal conditions for sequence coverage.
workflows.stages: 1. Extract scan headers from raw files using runScanHeadsman ;; 2. Import files and match fragments using readTopDownFiles ;; 3. Filter scans based on injection time deviation using filterInjectionTime ;; 4. Filter fragments based on CV using filterCv ;; 5. Filter fragments based on relative intensity using filterIntensity ;; 6. Aggregate technical replicates using aggregate ;; 7. Coerce to NCBSet to represent N- and C-terminal bonds ;; 8. Identify the best combinations of conditions using bestConditions ;; 9. Visualize coverage using fragmentationMap
workflows.code:
runScanHeadsman(
    path="path\\to\\raw-files",
    executable="path\\to\\ScanHeadsman.exe"
)

## the mass adduct for a proton
H <- 1.0078250321

myoglobin <- readTopDownFiles(
    ## directory path
    path = topdownrdata::topDownDataPath("myoglobin"),
    ## fragmentation types
    type = c("a", "b", "c", "x", "y", "z"),
    ## adducts (add -H/H to c/z and name
    ## them cmH/zpH (c minus H, z plus H)
    adducts = data.frame(
        mass=c(-H, H),
        to=c("c", "z"),
        name=c("cmH", "zpH")),
    ## initiator methionine removal
    modifications = "Met-loss",
    ## don't use neutral loss
    neutralLoss = NULL,
    ## tolerance for fragment matching
    tolerance = 5e-6,
    ## topdownrdata was generate with an older version of topdownr,
    ## the method files were generated with FilterString identification,
    ## use `conditions = "ScanDescription"` (default) for recent data.
    conditions = "FilterString"
)

## filtering on max deviation and just keep the
## 2 technical replicates per condition with the
## lowest deviation
myoglobin <- filterInjectionTime(
    myoglobin,
    maxDeviation = log2(3),
    keepTopN = 2
)

myoglobin <- filterCv(myoglobin, threshold=30)

myoglobin <- filterIntensity(myoglobin, threshold=0.1)

myoglobin <- aggregate(myoglobin)

myoglobinNcb <- as(myoglobin, "NCBSet")

bestConditions(myoglobinNcb, n=3)

sel <-
    myoglobinNcb$Mz == 707.3 &
    myoglobinNcb$AgcTarget == 1e6 &
    (myoglobinNcb$EtdReagentTarget == 1e7 &
     !is.na(myoglobinNcb$EtdReagentTarget))

myoglobinNcbSub <- myoglobinNcb[, sel]

fragmentationMap(
    myoglobinNcbSub,
    nCombinations = 10,
    labels = seq_len(ncol(myoglobinNcbSub))
)
